cards.text: In Proverbs, Wisdom calls out like a woman at the city gates, inviting anyone who'll listen (Proverbs 8:1-4). Now she has built her house and carved out her seven pillars. SEVEN pillars, friend, and my last home was a junk drawer propped up by takeout menus.
Then she prepares her meat, mixes her wine and sets her table. I know that energy, friend: that's me at 5 a.m. with every oven in the bakery warming up.

cards.question: Wisdom has built her house, prepared her meat, mixed her wine and set her table. What is all that getting ready for?
True or false: Once her table is set, Wisdom waits quietly inside until someone finds her house.

cards.text: She sends out her maidservants, and she calls out from the heights of the city. Wisdom put her invitation on a BILLBOARD, friend.

cards.question: Wisdom is calling out from the heights of the city. Who is her invitation for?

cards.text: She says, “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” and then, “Come, eat my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.” Lacking judgment is my whole résumé, friend, and she STILL wants me at her table.

cards.question: Wisdom's invitation comes with one thing her guests need to leave behind. What is it?
Wisdom makes a promise to the simple: leave your folly behind, and you will ___.

cards.text: Then the passage shifts to some straight talk: whoever corrects a mocker brings shame on himself, and whoever rebukes a wicked man taints himself. It's arguing with the reply-all guy, friend, and NOBODY leaves that thread clean.

cards.question: Proverbs 9 warns against rebuking a mocker. What will the mocker do if you rebuke him?
True or false: When you rebuke a wise man, he will love you.

cards.text: And then: “Instruct a wise man, and he will be wiser still; teach a righteous man, and he will increase his learning.” Give a wise man more to learn and he keeps growing, friend. He's the dough that RISES every time.
Then the passage digs down to the root of it all. The same verse says that knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.

cards.question: Right alongside that line about the Holy One, Proverbs 9:10 names the beginning of wisdom. What is it?

cards.text: There it is: “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom,” friend. Wisdom starts with God, not with a three-hour podcast.

cards.question: Then comes a promise: through wisdom your days will be multiplied, and ___ will be added to your life.
If you are ___, it's to your own advantage, but if you ___, you alone will bear the consequences.

cards.text: Now meet the other woman in this passage: “The woman named Folly is loud; she is naive and knows nothing.” Loud AND knows nothing, friend, that was me my first week in the bakery, yelling instructions at an oven that wasn't even on.

cards.question: True or false: Like Wisdom, Folly has a house of her own.

cards.text: She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the heights of the city, the same heights Wisdom called from. Wisdom carved seven pillars, friend, and Folly pulled up a CHAIR.

cards.question: From her seat, Folly calls out to the people passing by. What kind of people are they?

answers.text: Those leaving through the city gates

cards.question: When Folly calls out to the simple, she uses the ___ words Wisdom used.

cards.text: Word for word: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” Then she adds, “Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret is tasty!”

cards.question: Wisdom offered a feast she prepared herself. What is Folly's line about stolen water and secret bread really selling?
Folly's guests walk in expecting something sweet. What is really in her house?

cards.text: “But they do not know that the dead are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.” Two women, two houses, the same call to the simple, friend, and only one of those houses leads to life.

findings.problem: Card 2 has just told the baker that Wisdom prepared her meat, mixed her wine and set her table. That gives away the answer "A meal for her guests" and rules out "An offering at the temple" and "A harvest for the market." The card only asks the baker to restate what card 2 said.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 10 has just said that whoever corrects a mocker brings shame on himself. That setup rules out the wrong answers "Thank you" and "Obey you," so "Hate you" is the only answer left that fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "The same verse says that knowledge of the Holy One is understanding" reads as if it means the verse on card 13 (Proverbs 9:9). The line about the Holy One is in Proverbs 9:10, and no earlier card has introduced that verse yet. What he points out is not true as written.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: This card only repeats the answer the baker just gave on card 15 ("The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom"). It does not move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card hints that Folly calls to people who are keeping their paths straight. The answer goes against what a baker would expect, so the wrong answer "Those already lost and wandering" looks more likely than the right one. The baker can only get it by luck. Stop 2 already has other discovery questions (cards 2 and 5), so most of its choice cards are not informed guesses.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: This card quotes Proverbs 9:18 again right after card 8 has asked about it. It then sums up the whole passage ("Two women, two houses, the same call to the simple"). It tells nothing new, so it is a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
